title: Brief run compass — Kyla personal tally
content:
Purpose: quick handheld tracker for small-batch probe runs. Use this when iterating prompt+temperature or trying tiny quant/bs combos before promoting to phabricator ticket. Keep short; copy rows to team sheet if promising.

Legend: avg_latency_ms = median of 10 warm+steady calls; cost_est = rough $$$ per 1k input+output tokens using current pricing table; notes = immediate observations + next step flags (FOLLOWUP).

TABLE (compact):
run_id | date | model | quant | batch | mean_tok | avg_latency_ms | cost_per_1k | success_pct | notes
R-241  | 2024-09-18 | redwood-v1-small | 8bit | 1 | 58 | 84 ms | $0.72 | 92% | baseline prompt, clean outputs
R-242  | 2024-09-18 | redwood-v1-small | 8bit | 4 | 58 | 130 ms | $0.38 | 91% | batching helps throughput, watch latency tail
R-243  | 2024-09-19 | redwood-v1-small | fp16 | 8 | 58 | 290 ms | $0.35 | 90% | big batch, tail spikes on cold bins (FOLLOWUP: cache warm)
R-244  | 2024-09-20 | redwood-v1-medium | 8bit | 2 | 120 | 220 ms | $1.10 | 95% | quality improved on longer context
R-245  | 2024-10-02 | redwood-v1-small | q4_0 | 1 | 58 | 95 ms | $0.50 | 86% | hallucination on date parsing (REPRO)
R-251  | 2025-01-30 | redwood-v1-small | 8bit | 3 | 30 | 100 ms | $0.30 | 93% | short prompt, good latency/cost balance

Quick observations:
- Small batches (2–4) are the sweet spot for interactive latency while saving tokens compared to batch=1 on current autoscaler.
- q4_0 cuts cost but introduces subtle degradation on numeric/parsing tasks — mark as 'needs eval'.
- Tail lat spikes correlate with occasional large KV cache flushes; check SRE trace (link above).

Mini formulas / cheat sheet:
- cost_per_1k ≈ (model_rate_per_token * total_tokens) / 1000 — include both input+output. Use conservative 1.2x multiplier for retry overhead.
- apparent_throughput_rps ≈ batch_size / avg_latency_sec. Example: batch=4, latency=130ms => ~30 rps.

Next quick actions (short list):
1) Re-run R-245 with temperature=0.0 + fixed-system message to reproduce hallucination. (owner: Kyla)
2) Add R-242-like config to small shared shortlist for product demo (owner: Arjun).
3) Open a small regression eval if q4_0 shows >5% accuracy drop on parse prompts (owner: Mira).

Notes-to-self / TODOs:
- Consolidate runs older than 30 days into archived csv. Keep only top 10 wins in this sheet.
- When promoting, include a 100-sample eval set and cost/latency scatter plot.
- Ping SRE with traces for R-243 tail outliers (attach trace ids).

Rough timeline log:
- 2024-09-18: initial baseline runs, found batch=4 productive.
- 2024-10-02: observed q4_0 issues.
- 2025-01-30: short prompt optimization for demo.

Freeform scratch:
- Best prompt snippet: "System: you are a concise summarizer. User: <input>" gives tighter outputs, fewer tokens wasted.
- If we can get blocking latency under 80ms for batch=1 on small, it unlocks conversational demo. Keep that as aspirational metric.

References:
- Confluence: /display/ENG/mini-benchmarks (copy results before deleting)
- GH PR with perf tweaks (linked above)
- Slack thread: #mini-bench-discuss (see linked_artifacts)

Version notes: this is a personal working sheet — export to team drive before any obvious winners.
